Single Bench : Hon'ble Shri Rajeev Kumar Dubey, J.
 Misc. Criminal Case No.10660/2012
 M/s. Nirma Limited & Anr.
 vs.
 State of M.P. & Anr.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Shri Manikant Sharma, counsel for the applicants.
Shri Akhilendra Singh, Govt. Advocate for the respondents/State.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Order
Reserved on : 09/08/2018 Delivered on : 20/08/2018

This petition has been filed under Section 482 of CrPC against the order dated 13.08.2012 passed by Sessions Judge, Narsinghpur in Cr.R.No.83/2012 whereby he rejected the applicants' revision and affirmed the order dated 03.07.2012 passed by Judicial Magistrate First Class, Narsinghpur in Criminal Case No.31/2011.
Brief facts of the case which are relevant for just disposal of the present case are that on 07.07.2009 complainant, Food Inspector Sarika Choubey inspected the applicants/accused shop situated at Radha Vallabh Ward, Kareli, District Narsinghpur and took the sample of one packet of Nirma Pure Salt and sent it to Public Analyst who gave report that salt had been adulterated.

On that, written complaint against the applicants was filed on 07/01/11 and learned JMFC took cognizance against the applicants for the offence punishable under Section 7 (1) r/w 16 (1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act').

Applicants appeared before the trial Court on 13.01.2011 and filed an application under section 13(2) of the Act for sending second part of the sample of salt to Central Food Laboratory for re examination.

Learned Trial Court allowed that application by order dated 20.04.2012 and directed that second part of the sample be sent to Central Food Laboratory Ghaziabad for re examination on depositing draft of analysis fee by the applicant.

Applicant instead of depositing draft of analysis fee for sending second part of sample for analysis filed an application before trial court on 28/06/12 that the sample becomes unfit for analysis after expiry date of the sample.
Hence, the valuable right of the applicant given under Section 13 (2) of the Act is affected.
So the criminal proceedings pending against applicant be quashed.

sentences.text: Learned trial court rejected the application filed by the applicants on 03.07.2012 observing that just because it was mentioned on the sample that it was best for use only till two years from the date of its production, it cannot be said that the sample becomes unfit for analysis.
It could only be decided by the CFL.

Against this the applicants filed revision which too was dismissed by learned Sessions Judge vide order dated 13.08.2018 observing that impugned order is an interim order against which revision is not maintainable.
Being aggrieved from that order, applicants filed this petition.
Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that salt packet in question was best for use only till two years from the date of its production as printed on the packet.
The sample was taken on 07.07.2009 and complaint was filed by the complainant/non applicant before court on 07/01/11.
Applicant filed the application under section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act on 13.01.2011 well within time.
But prosecution took long time to file reply of that application and did not file reply up to 20/04/12.
In the meantime, shelf life of sample expired and sample became unfit for analysis.
The applicant could only exercise his right under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act within two years from the production of the sample i.e., 06/07/11.
After lapse of that period the sample was no longer in the food category.
Hence, the applicants' right given under Section 13 (2) of Act to re- analyze his sample has been violated.
So, the proceedings be quashed.
Learned trial court as well as learned revisional court committed mistake in rejecting applicant's application.

In this regard, learned counsel for the applicants also placed reliance on the Apex Court judgment passed in the case of Girishbhai Dahyabhai Shah vs. C.C. Jani & Another reported in (2009) 15 SCC 64 and State of Haryana vs. Unique Farmaid (P) Ltd. & Ors. reported in (1999) 8 SCC 190.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and submitted that the second part of the sample is yet to be analysed by the Central Food Laboratory without which it cannot be said that the accused has been denied of his right to get the second part of the sample analysed by the Central Food Testing Laboratory.
The applicant deliberately filed this petition with the intent to prolong the case and also got a stay, due to which the proceedings of the case in the Trial Court have stopped.
So only on the ground of delay, the proceedings of the trial cannot be quashed.
This Court has gone through the record and arguments put forth by the counsel for the parties.
It appears from the record that complainant/non applicant had filed the complaint well before the expiry period printed on the sample's packet.
It is the trial court who did not decide the applicant's application promptly.
The facts of the case relied by the learned counsel for the applicants do not match with the present case.
In the case of Girishbhai Dahyabhai Shah (supra) Food Inspector took sample of curd and notice of Section of 13(2) of the Act was served on the applicant after 15 months of taking the sample.
So Apex Court presumed that the sample had decomposed.
While in this case Food Inspector took sample of salt.
The second case is not related to the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
So these judgment do not help applicant much.

The question whether right of the accused has been denied or he has been deprived of his defence is not a matter of presumption or assumption and there must be material to show that the sample would not have remained fit for analysis by the time the applicant/accused had filed the application for quashing the proceedings of the case.

The expiration date is the date up to which the food M/S Nirma Limited vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193531852/

sentences.text: That means it's important to use that food before the expiry date to get the most nutritional value from it.

So just because the shelf life of food printed on the packet has expired, it cannot be said that sample becomes unfit for analysis for knowing the fact that whether the food sample is adulterated or not.

In the considered opinion of this court, applicant is not entitled to acquittal merely on the supposition that the sample must have decomposed and unfit for analysis when there is no such finding recorded by the CFL.

Apex Court in the case of Ajit Prasad Ram Krishna Singh v. State of Maharashtra reported in 1972 FAC 545 observed as thus:
"It is clear from the sub-section that the appellant should have made an application after paying the prescribed fee if he wanted the part of the sample available with him to be sent to the Director for analysis.

entities.text: Ajit Prasad Ram Krishna Singh v. State of Maharashtra reported in 1972 FAC 545
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If he had made the application after paying the prescribed fee, the Magistrate should, have had no option but to send the part of the sample for analysis by the Director.

If in pursuance of the application the part of the sample was sent to the Director and he had reported that the part of the sample was incapable of analysis for the reason that it was decomposed, the appellant could perhaps, have contended that he was deprived of his right to have the sample analysed by the Director on account of laches of the complainant and that he should be acquitted.
But, since the appellant never applied under Section 13(2) of the Act, he cannot complain that he has been deprived of any right.

In Babulal Hargovindas v.
State of Gujarat Jaganmohan Reddy, J. speaking for the Court, said that unless an application to send the sample to the Director is made, the vendor cannot complain that he was deprived of his right to have the sample analysed by the Director".

entities.text:
Babulal Hargovindas v.
State of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From the above judgement of Apex Court, it is clear that the question whether the sample was in a fit condition of analysis is a question of fact and depends upon so many circumstances.
The Courts cannot lay down any artificial rule that after the expiry of shelf life of sample, it must be presumed that the sample was not fit for analysis.
It has to be decided by the CFL.
While in this case the second part of the sample could not be sent to the CFL so far due to applicants' fault.
So it cannot be said that the sample would not have remained fit for analysis.
In these circumstance, both the learned courts below did not commit any mistake in rejecting the applicant's application.
Hence petition is rejected.

(Rajeev Kumar Dubey) Judge (ra) Date: 2018.08.21 11:42:17 +05'30'
